steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The Nazis believed in a racial hierarchy with the "Aryan" race (tall, blonde, blue-eyed Germans and Nordics) at the top as the "master race" (Herrenvolk). At the bottom were "sub-humans" (Untermenschen) - Jews, Roma, Slavs, and black people. Hitler wrote in Mein Kampf (1925): "The Jew is and remains the eternal enemy of the Aryan." | Key Fact: Persecution of Jews began immediately after Hitler became Chancellor. On 1 April 1933, the Nazis organised a nationwide boycott of Jewish shops and businesses. SA men stood outside Jewish shops with signs reading "Germans! Defend yourselves! Don't buy from Jews!" | Key Fact: At the Nuremberg Rally on 15 September 1935, Hitler announced two laws that fundamentally changed the legal status of German Jews: the Reich Citizenship Law and the Law

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain how the Nuremberg Laws affected the lives of German Jews. (4 marks) | Why was Kristallnacht a significant turning point? (8 marks) | "The persecution of the Jews escalated gradually between 1933 and 1945." How far do you agree? (12 marks)
